did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah sent a letter not only to the leaders of the exiles, but also to the priests, the prophets, and all the people who had been exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Did you know? The letter was sent after Jeconiah, the queen mother, the officials, and the craftsmen and metalworkers had been exiled from Jerusalem.
Did you know? The letter was delivered by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, who had been sent by Zedekiah king of Judah to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
Did you know? Jeremiah instructed the exiles to build houses and live in them, plant gardens, and eat their produce—in other words, to establish their lives even in exile.
Did you know? The exiles were instructed to seek the peace of the city to which they had been exiled and pray for it, because its peace would mean peace for them as well.
Did you know? Jeremiah warned the exiles not to believe the prophets, diviners, or dreams that promised them an immediate but false future.
Did you know? Jeremiah announced that the exile in Babylon would last seventy years, and only afterward would the LORD attend to His people and bring them back to their land.

Did you know? In the midst of the harsh reality of exile, the LORD promised His people thoughts of peace, a future, and hope—but this promise was given in the context of a long process, not immediate redemption.

Did you know? Jeremiah distinguished between the exiles in Babylon and those who remained in Jerusalem: those who remained would face sword, famine, plague, and further exile because they had not listened to the word of the LORD.

Did you know? Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah were condemned because they prophesied falsely in the name of the LORD and also committed adultery with their neighbors’ wives; their fate became a byword among the exiles of Judah.
